what: the blk_cnt work rebased onto comfy-kitchen v0.2.33 and built here, graded against upstream's own Sol test suite, with the stock PyPI 0.2.33 wheel as the control
why: ComfyUI moved its pin to comfy-kitchen==0.2.33 (core 18ebc2af) and the stock wheel replaced our 0.2.31+sol build. Everything we carried from kijai's branch is upstream by 0.2.33 (#117, #150, #156), so the fork's whole delta is the blk_cnt out-parameter the route observer reads. This is stage 1 of docs/research/2026-09-05_token_aug_plan.md, retargeted from kijai's PR head to the release that merged it.

rebase_target_moved.claim: the 2026-09-04 token_aug grade transfers to v0.2.33 unchanged
rebase_target_moved.evidence: kijai's graded head 1128df6 and the merge commit b678fdf have the identical tree 3e9736e; `git diff --stat 1128df6 b678fdf` is empty and `git diff --stat b678fdf~1 b678fdf` is not
rebase_target_moved.consequence: the plan's 'a moved head means the grade is redone' does not trigger

our_cases.result: 19 passed, 1 skipped (the HIP refusal case), 0 failed
our_cases.reading: every blk_cnt case upstream never had passes on a v0.2.33 base, direct path and chunked producer both

upstream_cases_that_fail_here.attribution: not ours: `git diff v0.2.33 HEAD` touches no .cu, .cpp, .cuh, .h, .hip, CMakeLists.txt, pyproject.toml or setup.py, and modifies none of these tests. Confirmed against the stock PyPI wheel, which fails the same cases.

cases.cause: the message it matches, 'workspace must be a uint8 array', is raised only by backends/hip/dlpack_bindings.cpp; the CUDA bindings carry no such check, so the test cannot pass on an NVIDIA card

cases.symptom: DID NOT RAISE RuntimeError, then an illegal memory access
cases.cause: same missing validation. The unrejected bad range then runs the kernel and raises cudaErrorIllegalAddress, which is STICKY: every later test in the same process fails at its first CUDA call, so one gap reads as dozens of failures

cases.symptom: cosine against the eager reference below the test's own 0.99 bar
cases.cause: not established here. The tie group straddling the top-k budget is not kept whole, which is what our own 2026-09-01 commit message recorded when it rewrote OUR tie test to state the spread rather than assert the whole group

stock_control.what: comfy-kitchen==0.2.33 from PyPI, unpacked to a scratch directory and put ahead on PYTHONPATH; the venv untouched
stock_control.tie_case_alone_in_a_fresh_process: fails on its own merits, not as collateral
stock_control.reading: identical to all printed digits, on the one case in the suite that compares the kernel to the eager reference and fails. The rebase changed no arithmetic RELATIVE TO STOCK 0.2.33, which is the comparand here and the only one this case can speak to. It says nothing about 0.2.31+sol, the build every Sol number in this repo was measured on -- see not_established below. It is also one case, not the capture footing stage 2 of the token_aug plan specifies.

how: tests are run from a COPY of the checkout's tests/ plus pytest.ini in a scratch directory. Run in place, pytest prepends the checkout root (tests/__init__.py makes tests a package), comfy_kitchen resolves to the source tree with no compiled extension, and all 119 cases skip while reporting success.

pytest is not in the ComfyUI venv and was not added to it: `PYTHONPATH=<venv>/lib/python3.13/site-packages uv run --no-project --python 3.13 --with pytest python -m pytest tests/test_sol_attn.py -q -o addopts=`
not_established: that the four upstream failures are failures on upstream's CI, which builds with its own flags on its own hardware. What is established is that they fail here on both the stock wheel and a local build, and that our commits cannot be the cause.

that a 0.2.33 base renders the same as the 0.2.31+sol build every Sol number in this repo was measured on. The kernel gained token routing (inert at token_aug=0) and a rope-cache change (#162, a weak ref where a strong ref was, so the freqs tensor is no longer retained). Nothing here rendered.

render_verification.what: the first render on the rebuilt kernel, with the route observer armed, so the node-to-kernel path is graded rather than assumed
render_verification.result: all graded assertions hold: 800 rows, 16 forwards at 16 distinct sigmas, every forward complete and routed as configured. The 11 in-window forwards route sol on all 50 DiT blocks; the 5 outside route composed_patch.
render_verification.blk_cnt_reached_the_kernel: yes. The raw uint16 sidecar filled and every sol row carries routed_density and kernel_density derived from the counts, so the out-parameter the rebase restored is filled by this build on a real render, not only in the unit cases.

smoke_h3_cannot_exercise_sol_at_its_defa.finding: bench/smoke_h3.py at its default --length 39 renders a 12,264-token sequence, and the shipped Sol node pins min_tokens 12288. Sol declines every call, so `sparse ran` reads MISSING on a healthy install, at any step count.
smoke_h3_cannot_exercise_sol_at_its_defa.not_the_cause: verbose. The smoke sets verbose=True on the node itself before submitting, so the log line is reachable; an earlier reading here blamed the graph's verbose=False and was wrong.
smoke_h3_cannot_exercise_sol_at_its_defa.shown: --length 49 gives 17,360 tokens and `sparse ran` reads ok on the same server and the same build
smoke_h3_cannot_exercise_sol_at_its_defa.consequence: a smoke run at the default length says nothing about the Sol path either way, which is the one path a kernel change puts at risk
